BiblicalUsage: mâshâh is to draw out, to pull from the water. In Exodus 2:10 Pharaoh's daughter calls the child Moses, because she drew him out of the water, and in 2 Samuel 22:17 and Psalms 18:16 David says God sent from above and drew him out of many waters. The word is the rescue that gives Moses his name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâshâh is the word of my own rescue. I hold that the God who drew Moses from the water draws me from the waters that would drown me.
